stories.headline: John Ternus Takes Over Apple With an AI Problem He Did Not Create
stories.key_takeaway: Apple's new CEO inherits a capex-light AI strategy that rents its most important capability from Google, and the company still has no public answer for what that costs at scale.

pull_quote.text: We'll see what Siri AI does from the cost side of it. There's also the ability when people use it a lot for them to move up on an iCloud Plan as well, and so what the balance of that is, is a bit uncertain at the moment.
pull_quote.role: Executive Chairman and former CEO, Apple

data_points.label: Apple's payment to Google for custom Gemini
Parameters in the licensed Gemini model
Parameters in Apple's own cloud models
Length of Tim Cook's CEO tenure

stories.article_excerpt: John Ternus spent 24 years at Apple learning how to make things Apple owns. On Tuesday he became chief executive of a company that rents its most important AI capability.

stories.headline: DeepSeek Is Closing a $7.4 Billion Round at $74 Billion — and Pointing at Shanghai
stories.key_takeaway: DeepSeek is raising about $7.4 billion at a $74 billion pre-money valuation to fund roughly a gigawatt of new compute, turning a hedge-fund side project into a capital-intensive company positioned for a Shanghai STAR Market IPO as soon as 2027.

pull_quote.text: DeepSeek's founding team, including Liang, are still traders at heart and inclined to chase maximum upside.

stories.article_excerpt: The company that once bragged about doing more with less is now raising one of the largest private financings in Chinese technology history.

stories.headline: Clay's Valuation Went From $1.25B to $7B in Eighteen Months. The Product Is a Spreadsheet.
stories.key_takeaway: Clay's jump to a $7B pre-money valuation led by Wellington, on just $204M ever raised and near-breakeven operations, shows investors will pay infrastructure-era multiples for capital-efficient AI application-layer software.

pull_quote.text: GTM engineering represents the first true AI-native profession, and we believe that it will be tech's next big job category.

stories.article_excerpt: In February 2025, Clay was worth $1.25 billion. On Sunday, Axios reported the New York company has inked a deal at $7 billion pre-money.

stories.headline: 17,800 Public AI Add-Ons, 6.7 Million Installs, No Vetting. AIR Just Raised $50M for That.
stories.key_takeaway: AIR Security launched from stealth with $50M across two seed rounds to police the unvetted skills, plugins and MCP servers enterprise AI agents install at runtime.

pull_quote.text: In the early 2000s, whenever you installed a driver, the driver didn't need to be signed. Today, every time you install a driver, you see a signature saying who signed it, because the driver is actually loading code into the kernel. You don't have that with skills or plug-ins or MCPs.

data_points.label: Total seed funding across two rounds
Public add-ons drawing from untrusted sources
Share of online skills AIR filters out

stories.article_excerpt: Somewhere in the enterprise software stack, an AI agent is quietly installing a skill it found on the open internet. Nobody signed it.

stories.headline: The GPUs Are Ready. The Buildings Are Not.
stories.key_takeaway: The AI buildout's binding constraint has shifted from chips to physical infrastructure, with 30-50% of planned 2026 data center capacity now projected to slip to 2028 while data centers absorb up to 70% of global memory output.

pull_quote.text: The magnitude of the price increase has exceeded our prior expectations and are headed even higher into next year.

data_points.label: World memory production going to data centers

stories.article_excerpt: The tightest bottleneck in artificial intelligence right now weighs several tons, contains no silicon, and has a three-year lead time.

stories.headline: Runway's Solaris Doesn't Write the App. It Renders It, Frame by Frame.
stories.key_takeaway: Runway's Solaris renders interactive UIs as generated video instead of code, and its own preference study looks strong — but there is no published latency number, no persistent state, no legible text and no ship date.

pull_quote.text: Video is the universal interface. Eventually, all UI will be chat and gestures in, chat and video out.

data_points.label: Preferred on natural behavior in scene

stories.article_excerpt: Pull a shirt off a rack and drag it onto a photo of yourself. The shirt lands. Nothing compiled to make that happen.

stories.headline: Z.ai's GLM-5.3-Flash Is the First Natively Multimodal GLM — and the Weights Are MIT
stories.key_takeaway: GLM-5.3-Flash pairs a permissive MIT licence with $0.15/$0.50 pricing that undercuts every rival open-weight model, served on what Z.ai says was entirely domestic Chinese silicon.

pull_quote.text: One caveat: the model is very chatty and burns a lot of tokens. Because the inference costs are so low, though, that's not too much of an issue.
pull_quote.role: Senior Editor for AI, The New Stack

stories.article_excerpt: For a week in late August, the most-used coding model on OpenRouter was one nobody could name. It went by ox-alpha.

stories.headline: Khanmigo Can Now Draw. Google Spent Six Months Making That Work.
stories.key_takeaway: Google embedded six engineers inside Khan Academy for six months to ship Gemini-powered interactive diagrams and teacher-reviewed practice tools, a launch that reads less like a feature drop than a targeted fix for the low-usage problem an independent RCT just documented.

pull_quote.text: The Google.org Fellows have supercharged our engineering effort, allowing us to produce several new AI-powered features in time for students and teachers to use these tools in the new school year.

data_points.label: Math gain for sustained participation, NBER RCT
Scope of the Hamilton County, Tennessee trial

stories.article_excerpt: For three years, Khanmigo could explain a parabola. It could not draw one. As of back-to-school 2026, it can.

stories.headline: Alibaba's Wan3.0 Makes 30 Seconds of 1080p Video With Sound in One Call — But There Are No Weights to Download
stories.key_takeaway: Wan3.0's 30-second 1080p video-with-native-audio specs are confirmed by Alibaba's own docs, but contrary to the Wan family's history it shipped closed — no weights, no repo, no published licence.

pull_quote.text: Open weights is not some kind of one-time philanthropic fluke for us. It's the strategy.

data_points.label: Formal release date, after Aug 6 beta

stories.article_excerpt: Alibaba's Wan3.0 will hand you 30 seconds of 1080p video with dialogue, music and sound effects from a single API call.

stories.headline: Given Only a Bibliography, Frontier Models Recover 3% of a Paper's Idea
stories.key_takeaway: On a contamination-resistant benchmark that gives models only a paper's pre-publication bibliography, seven frontier models recovered the actual research idea just 3-15% of the time, and a multi-agent tournament pipeline topped out at 42%.

pull_quote.text: This is a post-selected ensemble relative to the same papers used for scoring; we therefore interpret multi-agent results as evaluating this fixed top 4 roster rather than a selection rule validated on a held-out split.

data_points.label: ICML 2026 Oral papers in the ML slice

stories.article_excerpt: Strip a research paper away and leave only its footnotes. That is the entire input in Reconstruction, a blind benchmark posted in August.

stories.headline: The Honest Ledger on AI Drug Discovery: Structure Solved, Clinic Unproven
stories.key_takeaway: AI has decisively solved the upstream, data-rich parts of drug discovery, but a 2026 Nature Reviews Drug Discovery audit finds evidence of clinically relevant impact still limited, with AI-originated drugs clearing Phase 2 at the same ~40% rate as everyone else.

pull_quote.text: The sample size in each patient group was relatively limited, and these findings will need to be validated in larger cohort studies.

data_points.label: Phase 2 success — same as conventional drugs
FVC gain on 60mg rentosertib at 12 weeks
Projected end-to-end clinical success with AI

stories.article_excerpt: The most-read paper in AI drug discovery this summer is not a victory lap. It is an audit, and the audit does not balance.

stories.headline: AI Agents Keep Failing Because They Can't Predict What Happens Next
stories.key_takeaway: A 2026 research thread argues LLM agents fail on long-horizon tasks because they act without simulating consequences, and that an explicit text world model measurably improves web and embodied benchmarks — but only where the reward can itself be verified.

pull_quote.text: Yet despite their fluency, many such agents remain largely reactive: each step maps the current observation to the next action, without an explicit and inspectable account of the environment as a structured, evolving system.
pull_quote.role: Southern University of Science and Technology

data_points.label: WALL-E 2.0 success on ALFWorld after four iterations
Robotics domain score after DynDiff-GRPO, from 83.87

stories.article_excerpt: The most expensive mistake an AI agent makes is rarely the one you can see. It is the click three steps back.

stories.headline: The Pentagon Now Runs ChatGPT and Grok Side by Side for Three Million People
stories.key_takeaway: The Pentagon put ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government alongside Gemini on GenAI.mil for 3 million personnel at Impact Level 5, making vendor guardrail negotiations — not model capability — the decisive variable in defense AI procurement.

pull_quote.text: I am concerned that Grok's apparent lack of adequate guardrails could pose serious risks to the safety of U.S. military personnel and to the cybersecurity of classified systems.
pull_quote.role: U.S. Senator (D-Mass.), Senate Armed Services Committee

data_points.label: Max value of each defense AI contract

stories.article_excerpt: On Monday, the Pentagon quietly became the largest enterprise deployment of frontier AI in the world.

stories.headline: Anthropic Won in Court. The Pentagon Is Still Leaving by September 30.
stories.key_takeaway: Judge Rita Lin vacated the Pentagon's unlawful supply-chain-risk designation of Anthropic, but the ruling does not compel the department to buy Claude — and the migration off Anthropic's models is still on track to finish September 30, 2026.

pull_quote.text: The ruling does not require anyone to continue using Anthropic's products.
pull_quote.role: Government contracts attorney, Bradley Arant Boult Cummings LLP

data_points.label: Estimated value of the terminated contract
Unique GenAI.mil users of a 3M workforce

stories.article_excerpt: On August 27, a federal judge in San Francisco told the Department of War that it had broken the law. It changed almost nothing.

stories.headline: One Month Into Real Fines, the EU AI Act's Teeth Are Aimed at Disclosure
stories.key_takeaway: A month after the EU AI Act's enforcement powers switched on, no formal GPAI proceeding has been publicly opened — the only rules biting today are Article 50's chatbot and deepfake disclosure duties.

pull_quote.text: The AI Act gives innovators legal certainty while protecting the public interest.
pull_quote.role: Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, European Commission

data_points.label: Max GPAI fine as share of worldwide turnover
Max fine for prohibited AI practices

stories.article_excerpt: One month into the EU AI Act's enforcement era, the most powerful regulator in AI has not fined anyone.

stories.headline: The AI Red Lines Campaign Set Itself a Deadline. It Has Four Months Left.

sources.name: Global Call for AI Red Lines

stories.key_takeaway: Eleven months after 300+ signatories demanded binding international AI prohibitions by the end of 2026, the UN has built the machinery but no government has tabled a single binding red line, and the United States has rejected the premise outright.

pull_quote.text: We totally reject all efforts by international bodies to assert centralized control and global governance of AI.
pull_quote.role: Director, White House Office of Science and Technology Policy

data_points.label: Members of the UN scientific panel on AI
Countries endorsing the New Delhi Declaration

stories.article_excerpt: When Maria Ressa announced the campaign from the UN podium, it did something most open letters avoid: it wrote a date into its own text.
